comments.rawMarkdown:
All submissions are considered across all tracks but you are welcome to make it explicit if you prefer! 

Our internal process will involve multiple judges for the top papers so we anticipate ties being extremely unlikely. We can always add more judges to get a more refined score. If it does come to a tie break, it would likely be by original submission time, but again, we will prefer to avoid that. 

The full pipeline does not need to run when doing run all. We will likely look at any code that is present, but running the code itself is not guaranteed to be part of the evaluation process. With that being said, having a quick way to run your code sounds like a good idea to me.

firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Hello @elanmarkowitz, @ashleyoldacre, and the Organizing Team,

Thank you for organizing this competition and for answering questions across the forum. I would appreciate a brief clarification on three procedural points regarding submission evaluation:

1. **Prize Track Categorization (Best Paper vs. Best New Resource / Application):**  
   If a submission includes both empirical research findings and a new open resource (such as a curated trajectory dataset and evaluation sandbox), are all submissions automatically considered across all prize tracks (Overall Best Paper, Best New Resource, and Best New Application), or do authors need to explicitly declare a single target track in their Writeup?

2. **Edits and the Tie-Breaker Timestamp Rule:**  
   The rules state that *"in the event of a tie, the Paper that was entered first to the Competition will be the winner."* If a Writeup is entered early and subsequently updated with minor formatting adjustments or typos before the deadline, is the tie-breaker determined by the initial submission timestamp or the last modified timestamp?

3. **Notebook Execution Time for Verifiability:**  
   For evaluating the *Verifiability* criterion on attached Public Notebooks, do judges prefer a fast default execution mode (e.g., verifying evaluation benchmarks, unit tests, and pre-computed figures within a few minutes) while keeping multi-hour training/fine-tuning scripts optional, or should the entire pipeline run end-to-end on "Run All"?

Thank you for your time and guidance!
